fixes.explanation: Nothing in the passage says the rivers dry up, friend. Verse 10 has a river flowing out of Eden to water the garden, and verses 11-14 name the rivers that follow. The thing the LORD God calls not good is something else: “It is not good for the man to be alone.” (Genesis 2:18)

Good guess, since plants do love sunshine. But verse 5 doesn't mention the sun at all. What it says is that the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.

Roots are a fair guess in a garden story, friend. But verse 7 says the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and roots aren't mentioned there. Dust is the word the text uses, so that's the one that fits the blank.

This one is true, friend. Verse 9 says, “Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food.” The card says it in its own words, but the meaning matches. Every tree pleasing to the eye and good for food, and the LORD God is the One who gave it growth.

That's the one, baker! Verse 15 says the LORD God placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it. The man has real work to do from the start. A job with a purpose beats a Monday with nothing on the calendar, if you ask me.

You got it, baker! The LORD God says, “…but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil…” (Genesis 2:17). Out of a whole garden of trees, one gets that warning. Verse 9 puts that tree in the middle of the garden, along with the tree of life. Everything else is open, because the LORD God also says, “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden…” (Genesis 2:16).

That tree isn't in this passage, friend. Genesis 21:33 tells of a tamarisk tree planted at Beersheba by Abraham, a man we meet later in Genesis. That's a different story from the garden. In Eden, the LORD God says, “…but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil…” (Genesis 2:17).

Yes, baker! The LORD God says, “It is not good for the man to be alone.” Think about it. The garden has trees pleasing to the eye and a river watering it, and the one thing the LORD God points to is that the man is by himself.

Careful, friend, this one is true. Verse 24 says, “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife…” Right before it, in verse 23, the man speaks about the woman, and then verse 24 follows. Plain statements can feel like a trick, and I've side-eyed a plain truth or two myself.
